Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — WebCompass, a multimodal web-coding benchmark (text, image, video inputs; generation, editing, repair; 7 task categories, 1,526 tasks) with checklist-guided LLM-as-a-Judge for editing/repair and a new Agent-as-a-Judge (Claude Code + Chrome DevTools MCP) for generation; ten models compared

No SDD approach. Configurations are models only, agent not stated (models produce a repository or a patch from the task input): Claude-Opus-4.5, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, Gemini-3-Flash-Preview, GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct/-Thinking, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking/-Instruct; auxiliary Qwen3-32B (text-only comparison). Judge: Claude Code v2.0.67 with Chrome DevTools MCP Server v0.19.0, Claude-Opus-4.5 as judge model

Text-guided generation input: structured web design document (page content, interaction behaviours, visual appearance) elaborated by an LLM acting as product manager from underspecified queries. Editing: requirements stating what to change without implementation details ('specify goals, not methods'). Repair: vague defect hints, ground-truth search/replace annotations. Evaluation: LLM-generated checklist (task, operation sequence, expected result, criteria, max score)

N/A for the evaluated models (one output per task: repository for generation, patch for editing/repair). Agent-as-a-Judge: checklist generation -> browser interaction -> adaptive code verification (synthesised JavaScript tests, selector-only adaptation) -> evidence-grounded scoring
None in generation by the models; humans in dataset curation (expert review of all instances, recording videos) and in judge validation (200-sample subset)
Not an SDD workflow; models evaluated on the benchmark
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'structured web design document', 'specify goals, not methods', 'Spec Implementation' dimension

Both: new project (text-, vision- and video-guided generation of a complete web code repository) and existing code base (text/vision-guided editing and diagnostic/visual-diagnostic repair via patches on prototypes of 32k-64k characters)

1,526 tasks: 123 text-guided, 109 vision-guided, 94 video-guided generation; 300 each for text-guided editing, vision-guided editing, diagnostic repair, visual-diagnostic repair; 50 curated prototypes (single- and multi-page variants); Easy/Medium/Hard labels. Framework subset: 180 tasks (60 per category) x React/Vue/Vanilla

Front-end web development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript; React, Vue, Vanilla); 15 generation domains (e.g. e-commerce and fintech, enterprise, games, education), 16 editing operation types, 11 repair defect types
N/A (model outputs; annotators for curation and judge validation not described)
None for the evaluated models; judge cost per sample only (Claude-Opus-4.5 $4.66, Sonnet-4.5 $2.34, Haiku-4.5 $1.02)

0-100 scores per dimension (harmonic mean of normalised checklist items, epsilon = 1 smoothing). Generation: Runnability (RUN), Spec Implementation (SPI); Editing: Instruction Targeting (ITG), Feature Integrity (FTI); Repair: Root-Cause Targeting (RCT), Interaction Integrity (ITI); Overall = arithmetic mean of nine dimensions; Pass@1 and Worst-of-n (W@2, W@4)
Patch complexity (changed lines, patch count/hunks), repair patches compared with human ground truth
None

Visual dimensions: Design Quality (DSQ), Style Conformance (STC), Reference Fidelity (RFF); scores by difficulty, framework, subtask type, thinking vs instruct, text-only vs vision-language; error taxonomy (15 types in 4 domains plus repair-specific E5.x) with root causes; judge-human agreement (Pearson r, rank differences)

Editing/repair: patches applied, project launched in headless Chromium, screenshots and logs scored by LLM judge against a checklist (0-10 per dimension, structured JSON). Generation: Agent-as-a-Judge (Claude Code + Chrome DevTools MCP) runs the site, interacts, synthesises JavaScript tests; scores without auditable evidence discarded. Judge chosen by agreement with humans on 200 samples (Opus-4.5 r = 0.93-0.96). Error classification by LLM prompt

Tasks: same 1,526 WebCompass instances for all ten models; subsets for framework (180 tasks x React/Vue/Vanilla, four models), text-only comparison, thinking vs instruct, Worst-of-4 (two models). Baseline: none designated; repair has ground-truth patches and fixed screenshots. Held constant: inputs, judge (Claude-Opus-4.5), evaluation environment (Linux, headless Chromium, per-task timeouts). Acceptance criteria: LLM-generated checklists scored by LLM or agent judge; no deterministic test suites except patch applicability. Repetitions: single sample (Pass@1) for main results; n = 4 for two models. No statistical tests. Human intervention: none

Claude-Opus-4.5 (67.40) and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview (66.68) best, with complementary strengths (Opus leads RUN and ITG; Gemini leads RCT and RFF); best open model Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct 41.14, over 26 points behind; 30B models below half the top scores. Generation/editing ordering executability > functional > visual for closed models; repair ITI >> RFF > RCT. Editing especially hard for open models (18-28). Vanilla best for generation/editing, Vue weakest; GPT-5.2 best repair with React. Scores fall with difficulty (Gemini-3-Pro SPI 89.83 Easy -> 37.64 Hard). Animation edits and semantic-error repairs hardest. Thinking mode raises RUN but lowers SPI for 235B (35.02 vs 42.14). Feature Missing and Resource Fail are 40-55% of generation errors; Defect Not Addressed dominates repair errors (49-74%)

Distinguished models, task types, frameworks and difficulty levels; judge agreement with humans r = 0.93-0.96 (Opus-4.5) and model rankings within one rank of human rankings. Repeatability: main results single-sample; Worst-of-4 shows notable drops (e.g. Qwen3-VL-235B retains ~69.5%). Limitations stated: cannot keep pace with highly dynamic pages (games, timing-dependent animation); static benchmark with contamination risk; Agent-as-a-Judge is expensive; structured design documents test instruction following rather than creative intent

Front-end only (no back-end, database, API, deployment); structured queries trade creative-intent assessment for determinism; limited real-time interaction with dynamic pages; static benchmark contamination risk; evaluation cost of Agent-as-a-Judge. Gaps: visual design understanding, output consistency, holistic evaluation of user-facing artefacts

Inconsistencies: text says the visual dimension is the lowest axis in Generation for all ten models, but in Table 3 SPI is below DSQ for Gemini-3-Pro (55.76 vs 64.07), Gemini-3-Flash, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and all Qwen models; difficulty analysis names 'Gemini-2.5 Pro', not an evaluated model; Worst-of-n Pass@1 values (Table 8, e.g. Gemini ITG 74.84, RCT 50.95) match the Vanilla framework subset (Table 6), not Table 3, and the subset is not stated; conclusion '~25 points' vs 'over 26 points' (67.40 vs 41.14); Figure 8 uses harmonic mean of three dimensions while Table 3 Overall is an arithmetic mean of nine. Claude-Opus-4.5 is both an evaluated model and the judge (Claude Code orchestrator), a self-preference risk not discussed. Inference settings of the evaluated models (agentic or single call, temperature, limits) not stated. Values from Tables 3, 4, 5, 8 (pp. 11-12, 18, 27). Data: dataset on Hugging Face (NJU-LINK/WebCompass), code on GitHub, project page. Pre-registration: not stated. Programming languages: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (React, Vue, Vanilla)
